Which codes or function will give us correlation coefficients among latent variables and their p-values and 95% CI?

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: correlations among latent variables and plot
parts:
For correlation with p-value, you can use standardizedSolution(). (https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/man/standardizedSolution.html)

I haven't used corrplot and I am not familiar with it. It seems that it works on a matrix of correlations. If this is how it works, you can use lavInspect() with what = "cor.lv" to get the correlatiions for latent variables as a matrix (https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/man/lavInspect.html). You can then pass the matrix to corrplot().

This is an illustration:

``` r
# Adapted from the example of cfa()
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-17
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit <- cfa(HS.model,
           data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
# Get correlations with p-values
std <- standardizedSolution(fit)
std[(std$rhs %in% lavNames(fit, "lv")) & std$op == "~~" & !is.na(std$z), ]
#>        lhs op     rhs est.std    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 22  visual ~~ textual   0.459 0.064 7.189      0    0.334    0.584
#> 23  visual ~~   speed   0.471 0.073 6.461      0    0.328    0.613
#> 24 textual ~~   speed   0.283 0.069 4.117      0    0.148    0.418

# Get correlations as a matrix for corrplot
fit_cor_lv <- lavInspect(fit, "cor.lv")
fit_cor_lv
#>         visual textul speed
#> visual   1.000            
#> textual  0.459  1.000      
#> speed    0.471  0.283 1.000

library(corrplot)
#> corrplot 0.92 loaded
corrplot(fit_cor_lv)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/AxTjsUc.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2024-03-29 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai
